KnowledgeArticle.Title: Noise from Vehicle
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report noise from a vehicle, including horn honking, engine idling, or loud music.

Section.Name: 911 Noise from Vehicle
Section.Content:
Call 911
Call 911 to report:   
  • A car accident
  • Drag racing in progress
  • An all-terrain vehicle (ATV) in use
  • An unregistered dirt bike currently being driven on a City street
  • A car alarm going off

Need something else?

  • Noise Complaints to report other types of noise from vehicles

You can report noise from a vehicle caused by an idling engine, loud music, or horn honking. Horn honking is only allowed as a warning of danger.

What Happens Next

Officers from the New York Police Department (NYPD) will respond within 8 hours when they are not handling emergencies. They will be able to take action if the noise is still happening when they arrive. 

Legal Noise Limits

There is a limit to the amount of noise a vehicle's muffler or exhaust system may make on public roads where the speed limit is 35 miles per hour or less. According to New York City's Noise Code, sound is too loud if it can be heard:

  • From 150 feet or more from a vehicle weighing less than 10,000 pounds
  • From 200 feet or more from a vehicle weighing more than 10,000 pounds
  • From 200 feet from a motorcycle

Section.Name: DEP NYC Noise App
Section.Content:
NYC Noise is New York City’s Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) free iPhone and Android mobile app. The app will collect noise data for DEP to better understand noise levels, sources, and patterns.

The app does not submit noise complaint services requests.

NYC Noise is for data collection only. It provides DEP with:

  • Noise decibel level
  • Date, time, and source of noise
  • Defines noise by types:
    • Alarm
    • Car and bus traffic
    • Construction
    • Dog/animal
    • HVAC/fan
    • Loud music
    • Siren
    • Vehicle horn

Submitted data appears in map and table formats. Data will help DEP identify noise hotspots and guide their targeted enforcement efforts.

Learn more about DEP's NYC Noise App.
